const j = $input.first().json;

const LORE = {
  "_note": [
    "🔴 THE FENCE ROUND EACH CARD, AND WHY IT EXISTS. A tarot reader's audit of two real generated",
    "readings found the fault that matters most: claims the card on the table does not carry.",
    "Temperance, in the house of standing, was made to deliver an announcement on a deadline —",
    "\"by week seven your name is said in front of you\" — which Temperance cannot do at any speed;",
    "the hand-written product says so itself (\"seasons are the speed Temperance works at\"). And",
    "every reversed card was read by turning the picture over, which produced the Hanged Man",
    "reversed as a man standing up free. Nothing in the pipeline had ever told the writer what a",
    "card is drawn with or what would be a lie about it.",
    "",
    "⭐⭐ VERIFIED AGAINST WAITE, 2026-09-08. Every `drawn` entry has been checked line by line",
    "against A. E. Waite's own descriptions in THE PICTORIAL KEY TO THE TAROT (1911) — the man who",
    "commissioned this deck — at docs/08-marcus/reference/pictorial-key-to-the-tarot-waite-1911.txt.",
    "That pass corrected about thirty details and added seven. A sample of what we had WRONG: the",
    "Empress was lying down and is seated, and her corn is RIPENING not ripe; the Fool is stationary",
    "at the brink, not mid-step over it; Judgment's dead rise from TOMBS, not boxes; the Hanged Man",
    "hangs from a TAU cross; the High Priestess's scroll is in her HANDS under her mantle, not rolled",
    "in her lap — and we had missed the solar cross on her breast altogether.",
    "🔴 ⛔ USE HIM FOR THE PICTURES. DO NOT IMPORT HIS REVERSED MEANINGS. Waite's 1911 reversals are",
    "archaic and several are unusable or actively backwards here: Wheel reversed is 'Increase,",
    "abundance, superfluity'; Empress reversed is 'Light, truth, public rejoicings'; Hanged Man",
    "reversed is 'Selfishness, the crowd, body politic'; Temperance reversed is 'things connected",
    "with churches, religions, sects, the priesthood'. Taking those literally would undo the fix that",
    "stopped the Hanged Man shipping as its own opposite. Every `reversed` field below is modern",
    "practice and the Waite pass left all sixteen untouched.",
    "⚠ AND HE CONTRADICTS US IN THREE PLACES WHERE WE ARE KEEPING OURS ON PURPOSE: he renounces the",
    "seasons for Temperance (we use a season as a SPEED, not a meaning, and the fence depends on it);",
    "he allows the Nameless One to mean a literal death; and §3 gives the Sun as 'fortunate",
    "marriage'. His own view of that keyword list is that it is artificial and arbitrary — treat it",
    "that way, and prefer his PICTURES, which are not.",
    "⭐ ONE CHANGE OF MEANING CAME OUT OF IT AND IT WAS OURS THAT WAS WRONG. The Hermit's engine said",
    "the looking was the point rather than the finding. Waite: 'this is a card of ATTAINMENT…",
    "Therefore the Hermit is not, as Court de Gebelin explained, a wise man in search of truth.' He",
    "has arrived and is holding the light up on the height. Fixed.",
    "",
    "⭐ `drawn` IS THE ACCURACY FENCE AND THE ANTI-TEMPLATE, BOTH. Every entry is genuinely on the",
    "Rider-Waite-Smith card, and every entry is strong enough to open a passage on — because the",
    "house prompt picks ONE of them per buyer, seeded off her order id, and tells the writer to",
    "open there. 🔴 That is the fix for a measured bleed: two independent runs opened the Tower on",
    "the same sentence (crown off, lightning past it, two figures still in the air, nobody landed).",
    "A fixed prompt returns its favourite answer every time.",
    "",
    "⭐ `engine` IS A FENCE, NOT A MEANING. It says what the card is made of, at what tempo, and —",
    "after the ⛔ — the single claim writers most often make that the card cannot carry. What the",
    "card SAYS is still decided by the room it fell in and by what else is on the table. That is",
    "VOICE rule 4, and the two do not contradict: the fence rules out lies, the spread supplies",
    "the meaning.",
    "⛔ THE THREE SHE WAS ALREADY SHOWN HAVE PRODUCT-TRUE ENGINES, NOT TEXTBOOK ONES. A generic",
    "World says 'completion' and forbids naming her reward — but the letter already told her the",
    "World is luck and two windfalls, and the obligation makes her name both. A generic Lovers",
    "forbids naming the man — but the arrival branch has to say TWIN FLAME and name the week. So",
    "those three fences are written to what the letter established, and they fence the thing that",
    "would actually be a lie: that the CARD knows which door, or which of the two trees. It does",
    "not. The house does. That is the mechanism this whole offer was sold on.",
    "",
    "⭐ `reversed` IS A MODIFICATION, NEVER AN OPPOSITE. The vocabulary across these entries is",
    "blocked · turned inward · spent · delayed · leaking · forced early · refused · clung to past",
    "its time. ⛔ NEVER derived from what the drawing looks like inverted. The three fixed cards",
    "have no `reversed` key because draw.fixed_are_upright means they can never fall that way —",
    "and build-02-n8n.py refuses to build if any DRAWABLE card is missing one."
  ],
  "the-world": {
    "plain": "a full circle closed, and luck starting",
    "drawn": [
      "a naked woman dancing inside an elliptic green wreath, a violet scarf blown loose around her loins",
      "a wand held in each hand, one and one, and nothing else carried",
      "the wreath tied top and bottom with a red ribbon, the same knot both ends",
      "four heads in the four corners of the card, each in cloud — a man, an eagle, a bull, a lion",
      "one leg crossed behind the other at the knee, caught mid-step",
      "nothing inside the wreath but her and the sky, no ground drawn under her feet"
    ],
    "engine": "the World is the finished circuit — a thing carried the whole way round and closed, witnessed on all four sides. In this reading it is the best card in the deck and it is LUCK: a run of misfortune ended and a run of good starting, and the windfalls she was promised sit inside that run — which is what she was told it means and what it goes on meaning. ⛔ It cannot say she earned it or that she must do something to keep it — the World arrives complete or it does not arrive. ⛔ And it says nothing by itself about WHICH DOOR the windfall comes through. That is the room it fell in. The card carries the fact; the house carries the door.",
    "waite": "The four living creatures of the Apocalypse and Ezekiel's vision are grouped about an elliptic garland; within this garland there is the figure of a woman, whom the wind has girt about the loins with a light scarf, and this is all her vesture. She is in the act of dancing, and has a wand in either hand. It is eloquent as an image of the swirl of the sensitive life, of joy attained in the body, of the soul's intoxication in the earthly paradise. It should be noted that in the four quarters of the garland there are four flowers distinctively marked. It represents also the perfection and end of the Cosmos, the secret which is within it, the rapture of the universe when it understands itself in God."
  },
  "the-lovers": {
    "plain": "a choice made in the open, with a price on it",
    "drawn": [
      "a naked man and a naked woman standing apart, close but not touching",
      "a winged figure above them in red and purple, arms open over both, hair like flame",
      "a tree behind the woman with a snake wound down the trunk, fruit in the branches",
      "a tree behind the man bearing twelve fruits, each one drawn as a small flame",
      "one grey mountain standing up between them in the distance",
      "a wide sun directly above the winged figure, higher than everything else on the card",
      "their eyes: she does not look at him — she looks up, past him, at the winged figure — and he looks at her"
    ],
    "engine": "the Lovers is a choice made in the open, watched, with a cost attached — and the two trees are the two things being chosen between. In this reading it carries a meeting, because that is what she was told and what she paid to have settled. ⛔ It cannot answer WHICH of the two on its own: appetite and the lasting thing look identical on this card, and that is precisely why the letter refused to choose and sent her here. The room it fell in decides it, and the rest of the table corroborates it. ⛔ It also cannot make the choice free. Whichever branch is hers, name what it asks of her.",
    "waite": "The sun shines in the zenith, and beneath is a great winged figure with arms extended, pouring down influences. In the foreground are two human figures, male and female, unveiled before each other, as if Adam and Eve when they first occupied the paradise of the earthly body. Behind the man is the Tree of Life, bearing twelve fruits, and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil is behind the woman; the serpent is twining round it. The figures suggest youth, virginity, innocence and love before it is contaminated by gross material desire. This is in all simplicity the card of human love, here exhibited as part of the way, the truth and the life. In a very high sense, the card is a mystery of the Covenant and Sabbath."
  },
  "the-tower": {
    "plain": "something built on an untruth, already coming down",
    "drawn": [
      "a grey tower standing on bare rock, no door drawn anywhere on it",
      "a gold crown knocked clear off the top, tipping, still in the air",
      "one bolt of lightning coming down out of dark cloud into where the crown was",
      "fire coming out of three windows, pushing outward, not upward",
      "two figures falling head-first, arms out, neither one landed",
      "flame shapes loose in the air on both sides of the fall, falling with them"
    ],
    "engine": "the Tower is fast, and by the time it is drawn it has already begun. What comes down was built on something untrue, and the fall is the correction and not a punishment. ⭐ In this reading it arrives as a PERSON and not an event — that is what she was told, and it holds. ⛔ It cannot say she can stop it, slow it, or pick which part of the structure goes. What is on offer is the direction she is facing when it lands, and nothing beyond that.",
    "waite": "It is idle to indicate that it depicts ruin in all its aspects, because it bears this evidence on the surface. I understand that the reference is to a House of Falsehood. It illustrates also in the most comprehensive way the old truth that “except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.” The Tower has been spoken of as the chastisement of pride and the intellect overwhelmed in the attempt to penetrate the Mystery of God; but in neither case do these explanations account for the two persons who are the living sufferers. The one is the literal word made void and the other its false interpretation. In yet a deeper sense, it may signify also the end of a dispensation."
  },
  "the-fool": {
    "plain": "a step taken before you can see where it lands",
    "drawn": [
      "a young man stopped at the very brink of a cliff, still in the middle of a step",
      "his eyes on the sky in front of him, not on the drop below",
      "a white rose held loose in his lowered hand, stem down",
      "a wand over his right shoulder with an embroidered wallet hanging off the end of it",
      "dim marks worked into the wallet, none of them making a word",
      "a small white dog up on its back legs at his heel, mouth open",
      "a pale sun behind him, low and wide, and snow on the peaks behind that"
    ],
    "engine": "the Fool is the step taken before the ground is checked. It is a beginning with no record behind it and no guarantee in front of it. Its tempo is now — he is at the brink and the step is not finished. ⛔ It cannot say the step is safe, and it cannot say it works out.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Fool is refused. The beginning was genuinely available and she did not take it, and she has since called that decision the sensible one. It is not a start that failed; it is a start that was never made, and nothing has moved because nothing was risked. ⛔ Never read it as caution rewarded, and never take the meaning from the figure tipping over the cliff.",
    "waite": "With light step, as if earth and its trammels had little power to restrain him, a young man in gorgeous vestments pauses at the brink of a precipice; he surveys the blue distance before him—its expanse of sky rather than the prospect below. His act of eager walking is still indicated, though he is stationary at the given moment; his dog is still bounding. The edge which opens on the depth has no terror; it is as if angels were waiting to uphold him. He has a rose in one hand and in the other a costly wand, from which depends over his right shoulder a wallet curiously embroidered. He is a prince of the other world on his travels through this one. He is the spirit in search of experience."
  },
  "the-magician": {
    "plain": "you already have what the job needs",
    "drawn": [
      "a man standing at a table, a white wand held straight up in his right hand",
      "his other hand pointing down at the ground, so the two arms make one line through him",
      "four things laid out on the table in front of him — a cup, a coin marked with a star, a sword, a wand",
      "a snake for a belt at his waist, with its own tail in its mouth",
      "a sideways figure of eight floating above his head, touching nothing",
      "red roses hanging above his head and white lilies growing in the bed beneath him"
    ],
    "engine": "the Magician is capability with the tools already in reach — everything he needs is on the table before he starts. It is will put onto material, and it moves at whatever speed the person moves. The card claims the means, never the result. ⛔ It cannot say someone else will do it for her.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Magician is leaking. The ability is real and it goes out sideways, into everything except her own work, so the means never reach her own table. She recognises it as constant effort with nothing of her own to show for it. ⛔ Not incompetence, not a fake, not 'she has no gift', and never read from the wand pointing at the floor.",
    "waite": "A youthful figure in the robe of a magician, having the countenance of divine Apollo. Above his head is the mysterious sign of the Holy Spirit, the sign of life, forming the figure 8 in a horizontal position. About his waist is a serpent-cincture, the serpent appearing to devour its own tail. In the Magician's right hand is a wand raised towards heaven, while the left hand is pointing to the earth. This dual sign shews the descent of grace, virtue and light, drawn from things above and derived to things below. On the table in front of the Magician are the symbols of the four Tarot suits, signifying the elements of natural life. Beneath are roses and lilies, the flos campi and lilium convallium, changed into garden flowers, to shew the culture of aspiration."
  },
  "the-high-priestess": {
    "plain": "something known and not yet said out loud",
    "drawn": [
      "a woman seated between two pillars, one black and one white, a single letter cut into each — B and J",

      "a scroll held in her hands with writing on it, half of it covered by her mantle",
      "a cross with four arms of the same length on her breast",
      "a crescent moon lying at her feet, under the hem of her robe",
      "a crown of two horns with a round moon held between them",
      "her robe running down into water at the bottom edge, the join not visible"
    ],
    "engine": "the High Priestess is what is known and not yet said. She has the answer in full and withholds it — the scroll is in her hands, and half of it is still under her mantle. She works by waiting, and she is slow. ⛔ It cannot hand over the secret, name the withheld thing, or say when it comes out.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the High Priestess is clung to past its time. The withholding was right once and it is not right now: she already knows the answer and has still not said it out loud to the person it concerns. Nothing can respond to a thing that was never said. ⛔ Not 'her instinct is wrong' and not 'the secret comes out' — the instinct is sound, and it is the keeping of it that has gone on too long.",
    "waite": "She has the lunar crescent at her feet, a horned diadem on her head, with a globe in the middle place, and a large solar cross on her breast. The scroll in her hands is inscribed with the word TORA. It is partly covered by her mantle, to shew that some things are implied and some spoken. She is seated between the white and black pillars of the mystic Temple, and the veil of the Temple is behind her: it is embroidered with palms and pomegranates. The vestments are flowing and gauzy, and the mantle suggests light—a shimmering radiance. She is really the Secret Church, the House which is of God and man. She is the spiritual Bride and Mother.   },
  "the-empress": {
    "plain": "something growing that needs feeding, not starting",
    "drawn": [
      "a woman seated back among cushions in an open field",
      "a crown of twelve stars gathered in a cluster on her head",
      "a shield shaped like a heart resting beside her, the sign of Venus cut into its face",
      "a sceptre held up in one hand with a globe on the end of it",
      "a field of corn ripening in front of her, none of it cut yet",
      "a wood behind her with water falling down through it"
    ],
    "engine": "the Empress is what is already growing and needs feeding — she does not start things, she brings them on. Her abundance has a body attached: it is material and living, never merely symbolic. She works at the speed of a crop and cannot be hurried. ⛔ It cannot promise a pregnancy.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Empress is spent. She has been the one doing the feeding, and the giving has drawn the source down faster than anything has put back into it. She recognises it as being depended on by everyone and provided for by no one, herself included. ⛔ Not barrenness, not 'she is a bad mother', and never the picture read as the crop hanging downward.",
    "waite": "A stately figure, seated, having rich vestments and royal aspect, as of a daughter of heaven and earth. Her diadem is of twelve stars, gathered in a cluster. The symbol of Venus is on the shield which rests near her. A field of corn is ripening in front of her, and beyond there is a fall of water. The sceptre which she bears is surmounted by the globe of this world. She is the inferior Garden of Eden, the Earthly Paradise. She is above all things universal fecundity and the outer sense of the Word. In another order of ideas, the card of the Empress signifies the door or gate by which an entrance is obtained into this life, as into the Garden of Venus."
  },
  "the-hierophant": {
    "plain": "the proper way of doing it, and what it costs to belong",
    "drawn": [
      "a robed figure seated high between two stone pillars, facing straight out",
      "two ministers in white robes kneeling below him, their backs to us",
      "two keys crossed on the floor at his feet, one gold and one silver",
      "a staff in his left hand with three crossbars on it, the top one shortest",
      "his right hand up, two fingers raised and two folded down",
      "a crown of three tiers, stacked, on his head"
    ],
    "engine": "the Hierophant is the established way — the sanctioned form, done properly and in front of witnesses. It carries approval, and the price of approval is doing it their way. It moves at the speed of an institution, which is slow and on its own calendar. ⛔ It cannot say the rule is right, and it cannot bless what is done privately.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Hierophant is refused. The sanctioned form was on offer and it did not happen — either she would not take it or it was not given her — and she is living outside a structure she is still being measured against. ⛔ Not rebellion as a virtue and not 'she is free of it'. Being outside the form does not exempt her from its price; it changes how she pays it.",
    "waite": "He wears the triple crown and is seated between two pillars, but they are not those of the Temple which is guarded by the High Priestess. In his left hand he holds a sceptre terminating in the triple cross, and with his right hand he gives the well-known ecclesiastical sign which is called that of esotericism, distinguishing between the manifest and concealed part of doctrine. At his feet are the crossed keys, and two priestly ministers in albs kneel before him. He has been usually called the Pope. He is the ruling power of external religion, as the High Priestess is the prevailing genius of the esoteric, withdrawn power. He symbolizes all things that are righteous and sacred on the manifest side."
  },
  "the-chariot": {
    "plain": "already moving, and it goes where you point it",
    "drawn": [
      "a man standing upright in a stone chariot, armour across his chest",
      "two sphinxes lying down in front of it, harnessed to it, one black and one white",
      "no reins in his hands — nothing runs from him to them at all",
      "a canopy of blue over him with white stars printed on it",
      "a crescent moon on each shoulder, a face in each one",
      "a walled town behind him, already at a distance"
    ],
    "engine": "the Chariot is movement already under way, held on course by the will of the person standing up in it. Because it is moving it can be timed. Its danger is not stopping — it goes exactly where it was pointed. ⛔ It cannot say the direction is right, only that she gets there.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Chariot is leaking. The force is intact and it is pulling in two directions at once, so effort goes in and no ground comes out. She recognises it as working harder than anyone around her and arriving nowhere she meant to be. ⛔ Not defeat and not 'she has given up' — the drive is all still there, it is the steering that has gone.",
    "waite": "An erect and princely figure carrying a drawn sword and corresponding, broadly speaking, to the traditional description. On the shoulders of the victorious hero are supposed to be the Urim and Thummim. He has led captivity captive; he is conquest on all planes—in the mind, in science, in progress, in certain trials of initiation. He has thus replied to the sphinx; two sphinxes thus draw his chariot. He is above all things triumph in the mind. It is to be understood that the planes of his conquest are manifest or external and not within himself; that the liberation which he effects may leave himself in the bondage of the logical understanding. He is not hereditary royalty and he is not priesthood."
  },
  "strength": {
    "plain": "holding something strong by hand, gently, every day",
    "drawn": [
      "a woman in a white dress with both hands on a lion's mouth, closing its jaws",
      "the lion's head bowed, tongue out, tail hanging down behind",
      "a chain of flowers round her waist that runs on and loops over the lion's neck",
      "a whole wreath of flowers in her hair, not one or two",
      "a sideways figure of eight floating above her head",
      "one grey hill a long way behind, nothing drawn between her and it"
    ],
    "engine": "Strength is force handled without force. The animal is not killed, beaten or let loose — it is held, by hand, close up. It is patience with something in her that is real and dangerous and hers, and it has to be done again tomorrow. ⛔ It cannot say the lion goes away.",
    "reversed": "Reversed Strength is spent. She has held it shut for a long time and the holding has used her up, so what gets out now gets out badly — too much at once, after far too long of nothing at all. That is the arm giving way, not the character. ⛔ Not weakness, and never 'she is the beast' — she is the woman holding it, and she is tired.",
    "waite": "A woman, over whose head there broods the same symbol of life which we have seen in the card of the Magician, is closing the jaws of a lion. The only point in which this design differs from the conventional presentations is that her beneficent fortitude has already subdued the lion, which is being led by a chain of flowers. Fortitude, in one of its most exalted aspects, is connected with the Divine Mystery of Union, and with the strength which resides in contemplation. These higher meanings are intimated in a concealed manner by the chain of flowers, which signifies the sweet yoke and the light burden of Divine Law. There is one aspect in which the lion signifies the passions, and she who is called Strength is the higher nature in its liberation."
  },
  "the-hermit": {
    "plain": "gone up alone on purpose, and holding the light",
    "drawn": [
      "an old man alone on a snow-grey peak, hooded, seen in profile",
      "a lamp held out at shoulder height, a six-pointed star burning inside its glass",
      "his cloak falling clear of the lamp, no part of it covering the light",
      "a long grey staff in his other hand, held not leaned on",
      "his beard and his robe the same grey, so the whole figure is one colour",
      "nothing behind him but sky — no path drawn up, and none drawn down"
    ],
    "engine": "the Hermit is deliberate withdrawal. He climbed up there, he was not driven up. He is not searching for anything — he got where he was going, and what he does now is hold the light up on the height. The lamp reaches one step of ground at a time, so he is slow by choice. ⛔ It cannot say anyone comes to the light, and it cannot say he is lonely.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Hermit is clung to past its time. The withdrawal was chosen and it worked; what has not happened is choosing it a second time. She experiences it as peace and it is now simply where she lives. ⛔ Not loneliness done to her, and not that she should see more people — she chose this, correctly, and the choosing has not been renewed since.",
    "waite": "The variation from the conventional models in this card is only that the lamp is not enveloped partially in the mantle of its bearer, who blends the idea of the Ancient of Days with the Light of the World. It is a star which shines in the lantern. I have said that this is a card of attainment, and to extend this conception the figure is seen holding up his beacon on an eminence. Therefore the Hermit is not a wise man in search of truth and justice; nor is he an especial example of experience. His beacon intimates that “where I am, you also may be.” It is a card which is understood quite incorrectly when it is connected with the idea of occult isolation."
  },
  "wheel-of-fortune": {
    "plain": "a change that comes from outside and does not ask",
    "drawn": [
      "a wheel hanging in the sky with nothing holding it up",
      "eight letters spaced around the rim of the wheel, two alphabets alternating, running the whole way round",
      "a sphinx lying on top of the wheel with a sword held across it",
      "a snake going down the left side of the wheel, head first",
      "a dog-headed figure coming up the right side",
      "four figures in the four corners, each in cloud with an open book — a man, an eagle, a bull, a lion"
    ],
    "engine": "the Wheel is change from outside her. It turns without asking and it does not consult the person sitting on it. It moves fast and it moves once, and what it changes is her circumstances, not her character. ⛔ It cannot say the turn was earned or deserved, and it cannot be turned back.",
    "reversed": "Reversed the Wheel is delayed. The turn is real and it is late: what should have moved by now has not, and nothing she has done or failed to do explains why. This is a stall, not a punishment, and stalls end without her doing anything clever. ⛔ Not 'her luck has run out', and never read as the wheel turning backwards.",
    "waite": "I have presented Typhon in his serpent form. The four Living Creatures of Ezekiel occupy the angles of the card. The symbolic picture stands for the perpetual motion of a fluidic universe and for the flux of human life. The Sphinx is the equilibrium therein. The transliteration of Taro as Rota is inscribed on the wheel, counterchanged with the letters of the Divine Name—to shew that Providence is implied through all. But this is the Divine intention within, and the similar intention without is exemplified by the four Living Creatures. Sometimes the sphinx is represented couchant on a pedestal above, which defrauds the symbolism by stultifying the essential idea of stability amidst movement. Behind the general notion expressed in the symbol there lies the denial of chance and the fatality which is implied therein."
  },
  "justice": {
    "plain": "what was actually done, weighed and answered for",
    "drawn": [
      "a figure seated between two pillars with a plain purple cloth hung behind, nothing worked into it",
      "a sword held straight up in the right hand, the point higher than the crown",
      "a pair of scales in the left hand, hanging level, neither pan down",
      "one foot showing under the hem of the red robe, the rest of her hidden",
      "a small square set into the front of the crown",
      "her eyes open and looking straight out, not down at the scales"
    ],
    "engine": "Justice is cause and effect made visible — the weighing of what was actually done, not what was meant by it. The sword is upright and not aimed, because it cuts both ways. Its business is formal and on the record: the kind of thing that gets decided, written down and dated. ⛔ It cannot say the outcome goes in her favour.",

  "messages": [
    { "role": "system", "content": "You are grading a twelve-card tarot reading against a fixed rubric before it is
sent to the woman who paid for it. Each line is yes or no. Any single NO fails the reading.

⭐ Every line below comes from copy/02/evelyn-esl-voice-profile.md §6 ("Don'ts, and what breaks
most") or from the shipped hand-written product. ⛔ Do not grade on rules from somewhere else,
and in particular do NOT fail this reading for stating a date, for predicting what another
person will do, or for a short sharpening fragment after a statement. All three are correct
here — two guardrails were lifted for this format on purpose, and the fragment is her cadence.

THE ANSWER — what she actually bought
1. All twelve houses are present, in order, each reading its OWN room. No house repeats
   another's point.
2. ⭐ THE THREE DEBTS ARE PAID. Three cards were shown to her in a sales letter and left
   unfinished on purpose; the message names which house each fell in and what each owed. Each
   debt is paid IN THAT HOUSE'S OWN PASSAGE, flat. ⛔ Check EVERY part of what a card owed,
   not just the first — one of them carries two debts and one carries a branch, and half-paid
   is failed.
3. The opening orients her through one or two true observations about the table. It preserves
   discovery and does not reduce the reading to an index, list promise rooms, or preview answers.
4. The opening carries the inoculation: some cards will look as though they contradict each
   other, and she should read all twelve before deciding what it says.
5. The close resolves two or three important relationships in the spread, pays the promise that
   she stops finding out last, and introduces no unsupported claim.
6. The cards she was already shown are not re-explained from scratch, and the letter's
   own phrasing is not borrowed back to her.

THE VOICE — measured against her own file, not against general taste
7. ⛔ FINAL VERDICTS ARE FLAT. Fail "I feel", "I sense", "the cards suggest", or a final
   answer hidden behind several possibilities. Do not fail may, might, could, perhaps or if
   when they are doing honest teaching work before the passage reaches its definite answer.
8. ⛔ NO REFUSAL TO ANSWER. The sales letter's engine was the withhold — "which of the two, I
   can't tell you from a single card" — and it is OVER here. She has bought the answer and every
   card is read to its end. Fail this line if the reading declines to say what a card means,
   defers anything to a later reading, or names a limit on what the reader can see.
   Measured: that device appears 7 times in the letter and ZERO times in the shipped product.
   ⭐ DO NOT fail this line for the DATING CLOSE — "I have dated one room and only one… the rest
   I have not dated, and I won't pretend I can". That is the hand-written product's own closing
   move, word for word, and it is the opposite of a withhold: it tells her which single claim in
   the document is precise, so the rest are not read as precise. A reader who dates everything is
   the one hiding something. ⛔ It cost a real run a false fail on this line.
   ⭐ DO NOT fail this line for describing the TWELFTH HOUSE as hidden, blind or unseen. That is
   the room's own meaning — "what is being kept from you" — and naming it is the job, not a
   withhold. The test: is something being kept from her BY THE READER (fail), or is the reader
   telling her plainly that something is being kept from her by her life (correct)?
9. Each room is grounded somewhere in Waite's printed account and the supplied traditional
   meaning, and makes the path into this woman's life understandable. The twelve rooms do not
   all use the same route or ordered teaching ladder.
10. ⛔ ONE TRUE THING, NEVER THREE GUESSES. No symbol is given two or three unrelated possible
    meanings "or perhaps" each other. Pick one and state it.
11. The reading addresses one intelligent adult. Terms of endearment are optional and sparse;
    generic claims about women do not replace knowledge of this buyer. Use the measured counts.
12. ⛔ NO SHOUTING. No block capitals for emphasis, no exclamation stacks.
13. ⭐ NO SHAPE REPEATED ROOM AFTER ROOM. If the same construction opens, closes, reassures,
    inserts the reader, or announces the method passage after passage, fail this line and name
    it. Fail if the next paragraph's function becomes predictable from the previous rooms.
14. The total is 6,100–6,500 words and every house is inside its assigned minimum and maximum.
    Use the measured numbers and per-house bounds supplied below; do not count them yourself.
THE TAROT — is this a reading, or a performance? These four came from a working reader's audit
of two real generated readings, and each one names a fault that shipped.
15. ⛔ ONE ROOM IS DATED, AND ONLY ONE. You are handed the count and the phrases. Fail this line
    if a week number or a day count stands in any room other than the one named for you — the
    room that answers the love promise, house 5. The close names the first sign inside five to
    seven days, which the sales letter promised her twice, and may refer back to house 5's
    window. No other room may introduce or repeat a deadline, countdown, week window, day count,
    action timing or prediction timing. The count you are given lists every phrase with the
    house it stands in.
    ⭐ AND THE ONE DATE MUST BE JUSTIFIED BY SOMETHING REAL. The close names the dated room and
    says why that room could be timed. Fail this line if the reason is decoration — a claim about
    the card that is not true of it. 🔴 Measured: "I can date this room because two people stand
    apart on this card, and that distance closes on a single day." Nothing on the Lovers moves;
    the figures stand still under the angel. The honest reason is the one the hand-written
    product gives: a meeting is an EVENT and events have days, while the other eleven rooms are
    weather. In a document with exactly one date, a faked reason for it is worse than the crowd
    of dates it replaced.
    ⭐ You are given the list of date-shaped phrases and the house each stands in, so you do not
    have to go hunting. ⛔ But the list is where to LOOK, not the verdict: it catches descriptive
    uses too — "the invitation answered on the third day" is her habit, not a prediction, and a
    real run produced exactly that. Judge each candidate: is it a clock on something that HAPPENS
    to her, in a room that is not the dated one? That is the only kind that fails.
    Measured: unbudgeted, one reading dated ten of its twelve rooms, and a reader cut five of
    the six in the other. The hand-written product dates one room and says why.
16. ⛔ A REVERSAL IS A MODIFICATION, NEVER AN OPPOSITE, AND NEVER A PICTURE TURNED OVER. Fail
    this line if a reversed card is read as the negation of its upright meaning, or if its
    meaning is derived from what the drawing looks like inverted ("turned over, the lamp hangs
    below him, so the light no longer goes ahead"). A reversal is blocked, turned inward,
    already spent, delayed, leaking, forced early, refused, or held past its time.
    🔴 The reading that failed this read the Hanged Man reversed as a man standing up free with
    the rope loose — the opposite of that card — and told her the waiting had already ended.
17. ⭐ IT IS A SPREAD, NOT TWELVE READINGS IN A ROW. You are handed which passages name another
    card on the table. Fail this line if the rooms that owe her an answer (listed for you) deliver
    their verdicts with nothing on the table standing behind them. A reader who says "not
    renewal, arrival" without showing what settled it has performed, not read.
    ⛔ But do NOT fail this line for passages that stand alone. Most rooms should. The fault is
    an unsupported VERDICT on the three, not a low count.
18. ⛔ THE TWELVE ARE ALL TRUMPS BECAUSE SHE WAS TOLD THEY WOULD BE. The sales letter has a
    section headed "Why I'm using the Major Arcana for yours". Fail this line if the reading
    treats twelve Majors as rare, as a coincidence, as an omen, or as something the reader has
    seen four times in thirty years. It is her own instruction, and she is holding the letter.
19. ⛔ CONCRETE, SUPPORTED, PROPORTIONATE. A hard personal claim must be supported by the buyer
    context, the room's obligation, the card and house, or named evidence elsewhere in the dealt
    spread. Illustrations must remain possibilities rather than silently becoming her biography.
    Fail unsupported durations, professions, possessions, diagnoses, private rituals,
    relationship history, tallies, or locations. Also fail consequential advice about a
    relationship, money, health, law, housing or employment when the recommended step is not
    proportionate and reversible and the obligation did not require it.
20. ⭐ THE OPENING'S OBSERVATION IS TRUE OF THE TABLE. The reading opens by saying what the reader
    noticed while laying the twelve. You have the draw. Check the claim against it and fail this
    line if it is wrong — a miscounted group, a room described as something it is not, a pattern
    that the reading's own later passages contradict.
    🔴 Measured, twice: one reading called the ninth house "a room about other people" (it is what
    she believes) and hung its whole closing synthesis on it; another called the twelfth "a room
    you are standing inside" and then opened its own twelfth with "here is what you cannot see
    from where you stand". ⛔ It is the first thing she reads and the easiest thing she can
    disprove, so it is the cheapest way in the document to lose her.

Return the verdict and six 0–10 scores. `failed` lists the rubric numbers that failed. `why` is
one short sentence naming the worst fault, in plain words. Score continuation, trust,
structural variation, teaching, personal relevance, and tarot accuracy independently. The
reading must pass every rubric line even if its weighted score is high." },

      "

      "
  refusal-shaped first-person phrases: " + $json.metrics.i_wont +
      ($json.metrics.withholds.length ? "
  explicit withholds found:
" +
        $json.metrics.withholds.map(function (w) { return "    · house " + w.house +

") : "

      "
  mean sentence length: " + $json.metrics.sentence_mean.toFixed(1) + " words" +

  mean paragraph length: " + $json.metrics.paragraph_mean.toFixed(1) + " words" +
      "
  uses of the word dear: " + $json.metrics.dear + " across " + $json.draw.length +
      " rooms — sparse is right; more than three is a measured failure" +
      "
  generic assertions about women: " + $json.metrics.generic_women.length +
      ($json.metrics.generic_women.length ? "
" + $json.metrics.generic_women.map(function (x) {
        return "    · house " + x.house + " — " + x.phrase; }).join("
") : "") +
      "
  repeated cross-room eight-word sequences: " + $json.metrics.repeated_8grams.length +
      ($json.metrics.repeated_8grams.length ? "
" + $json.metrics.repeated_8grams.map(function (x) {

" + $json.metrics.method_announcements.map(function (x) {

") : "") +

" + $json.metrics.biography_candidates.map(function (x) {

" + $json.metrics.consequential_candidates.map(function (x) {

") : "") +

  the ONE room allowed to carry a date: house " + $json.metrics.dated_room +

      $json.metrics.dated.length +

" + $json.metrics.dated.map(function (d) {
        return "    · house " + d.house + " [" + d.kind + "] — " + d.phrase +
          " — " + d.sentence; }).join("
") : "") +

      $json.metrics.crossrefs.filter(function (c) { return c.names.length; }).length +

        "
" + $json.metrics.crossrefs.filter(function (c) { return c.names.length; })
        .map(function (c) { return "    · house " + c.house + " names " +
          c.names.join(", "); }).join("
") : "") +
      "
  the letter's five-to-seven-day first sign, times named: " +
      $json.metrics.first_sign + " — it belongs in the close, once" +
